second_speaker_utterance_with_correspond: Investments in technology and infrastructure in universal systems often fail to deliver consistent improvements due to bureaucratic inefficiencies.
The moral imperative of healthcare access is important, but it does not justify a system that struggles to provide timely and high-quality care for everyone.
Mixed models can ensure universal access while leveraging private sector efficiency to address systemic issues more effectively.
Occasional delays in universal systems are not trivial; they can lead to severe consequences for patients needing urgent care.
Why should we rely solely on a system that repeatedly fails to adapt when a balanced approach can achieve better outcomes for all?
